dhp146:1: Why laughter? why exultation? For the world is ever aflame.
dhp146:3: Will ye not seek a light, ye that are shrouded in darkness?
dhp147:1: See this painted image, this mass of sores, huddled together,
dhp147:3: Corrupt, once possessed of many thoughts, but now possessing neither strength nor stability.
dhp148:1: This body is worn out, this nest of disease, this fragile body;
dhp148:3: This mass of corruption dissolves; for life ends in death.
dhp149:1: Like yonder gourds cast away in the autumn
dhp149:3: Are these gray bones; what pleasure can there be in looking at them?
dhp150:1: It is a city made of bones, plastered with flesh and blood,
dhp150:3: Where lodge old age and death and pride and deceit.
dhp151:1: The gayly painted chariots of kings wear out; likewise does the body wear out.
dhp151:3: But the state of the good wears not away; the good proclaim this to the good.
dhp152:1: A man who has learned but little, grows old like an ox;
dhp152:3: His flesh increases, but his wisdom, not.
dhp153:1: Through a round of countless existences have I run to no purpose,
dhp153:3: Seeking the Builder of the House. Repeated birth is suffering.
dhp154:1: I see you, Builder of the House. You shall not build the house again.
dhp154:3: All your rafters are broken, and your ridge-pole is shattered.
dhp154:5: The mind, at rest in Nibbāna, has attained extinction of cravings.
dhp155:1: They that have not led the holy life, they that have not obtained wealth in time of youth,
dhp155:3: Perish like worn-out herons in a pond from which the fish have disappeared.
dhp156:1: They that have not led the holy life, they that have not obtained wealth in time of youth,
dhp156:3: Lie like worn-out bows, bewailing the times that are past.
